newsitem.title: USA: Feds appeal release of Hong Kong tobacco executive.
newsitem.headline: Feds appeal release of Hong Kong tobacco executive.

text.p: Federal prosecutors on Thursday appealed a judge's ruling that would have set free a Hong Kong tobacco company executive wanted there on charges of conspiracy and corruption.

The Hong Kong-born Lui Kin-hong was commerical director of the Hong Kong subsidiary of British-Amerian Tobacco Company (Hong Kong) Ltd, which had exclusive rights to distribute cigarettes in several Asian countries.

He has been fighting extradition since his December, 1995 arrest at Boston's Logan International Airport. Hong Kong officials have claimed that Lui accepted more than $3 million in cash bribes and $1.5 million in unsecured loans to ensure the supply of cigarettes to a distributor.

But U.S. District Judge Joseph Tauro ruled on Jan. 7 that federal prosecutors failed to prove the Crown Colony would have sufficient time to try and, if found guilty, punish Lui before July 1, 1997, when it reverts to China.
He ordered Lui released, but gave prosecutors up to 10 days to appeal his ruling.
Another hearing before Judge Tauro is set for Friday.

Lui's lawyer Harvey Silverglate said he expected his client to be released on bail and that he would stay in Boston to fight the appeal, which is to be heard before the 1st U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals.
"I think they are going to lose and they are going to create, from their point of view, an undesireable precedent, having a higher court," Silverglate told Reuters.
